identity.title: The Shape of Adversarial Influence: Characterizing LLM Latent Spaces with Persistent Homology

problem.claim: Characterize how adversarial inputs reshape the geometry and topology of LLM internal representation spaces.

gap.claim: Existing interpretability methods mainly capture linear directions or isolated features, overlooking high-dimensional, relational, nonlinear geometry; cross-attack topological effects remain poorly understood.

contributions.claim: Applies persistent homology to activation point clouds and neuron-level information flow to characterize adversarial representational change.
Reports a consistent topological signature across six models spanning 3.8B–70B parameters and two attack modes: indirect prompt injection and backdoor fine-tuning.
Defines adversarial topological compression as a shift from varied, compact, small-scale features toward fewer dominant, large-scale features.

stated_novelty.claim: The framework reveals geometric invariants of representational change that complement existing linear interpretability methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that a consistent topological signature persists across six models and both evaluated attack modes.
Authors report that the signature is architecture-agnostic, emerges early in the network, and is highly discriminative across layers.
Authors report that adversarial inputs induce topological compression in latent spaces.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing interpretability captures primarily linear directions or isolated features, missing nonlinear relational geometry.
Topological effects across operationally different attack modes are described as poorly understood.
The paper applies persistent homology to internal representations and analyzes activation geometry and neuron-level information flow.
Across six models and two attacks, the authors report persistent topological compression with an architecture-agnostic, early-emerging, layer-discriminative signature.

source_observation.claim: The paper combines persistent homology with activation point-cloud and neuron-level analyses to complement linear interpretability.

lessons.interpretation: A representation-change claim can become more informative when the analysis tool matches the claimed geometric structure.
lessons.application: For a nonlinear or relational representation hypothesis, pair linear probes with a topology- or geometry-sensitive analysis and state what each reveals.
lessons.exception: This pairing may be unsuitable when the research question concerns only a defined linear direction or when the data do not support meaningful geometric structure.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative effect sizes, statistical tests, or operational definitions for topological compression, persistence, or discriminativeness.
Details of model architectures, attack implementations, layers analyzed, and baselines are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or priority of the stated novelty.
